author: gbeshers
title: TargetInvocatonException while changing mouse point to "Inverted"

status.label: Actionable fix hypothesis
status.detail: The attached stack identifies a WPF theme refresh failure in PowerToys Run; the reported trigger and module description do not fully agree.

next_action.label: Reproduce Run theme refresh failure
next_action.reason: Confirm whether repeated system-theme notifications reapply the same WPF ThemeMode and trigger the duplicate resource-key exception.

judgment.rationale: The stack and attached text identify a concrete PowerToys Run theme-refresh path ending in a WPF duplicate SystemColorWindowColorBrush key. Current upstream ThemeManager handles every General user-preference notification by calling UpdateTheme, and SetSystemTheme assigns Application.Current.ThemeMode on each pass. That makes redundant theme reapplication a plausible fix target, but the issue labels PowerToys Run while its form describes a Mouse Utilities setting, and the reported 0.87.1.0 build is much older than current releases. This is a lightweight hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause or completed design.
evidence: The issue body reports PowerToys 0.87.1.0 on Windows 11 build 26200 and shows a TargetInvocationException while changing the pointer style to Inverted.

The stack runs through SystemEvents.UserPreferenceChanged, PowerLauncher.Helper.ThemeManager.OnUserPreferenceChanged, UpdateTheme, and SetSystemTheme before WPF throws that SystemColorWindowColorBrush is already present.
The linked 2026-09-29 text attachment contains the same duplicate-key exception and PowerToys Run ThemeManager stack.

Current upstream src/modules/launcher/PowerLauncher/Helper/ThemeManager.cs calls UpdateTheme for General preference changes and assigns Application.Current.ThemeMode in SetSystemTheme without checking whether the mode is already set.
The Product-PowerToys Run label and stack conflict with the report's Mouse Utilities wording, leaving the precise triggering transition uncertain.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the exact pointer-style/system-theme transition on the reported and a current build; if redundant WPF ThemeMode application reproduces the duplicate key, design a narrowly guarded refresh and a repeated-notification regression test.

fix_assessment.rationale: A repeated WPF application-theme refresh is a code-level hypothesis directly supported by the exception stack and the current Run theme handler, but the trigger mismatch and old reported version require reproduction before selecting the exact correction.

proposed_fixes.title: Avoid redundant WPF theme reapplication after system preference changes
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a General user-preference event causes PowerToys Run to reassign an unchanged Application ThemeMode, provoking WPF to reload a system theme dictionary that contains a duplicate SystemColorWindowColorBrush key.
plan: Reproduce the reported pointer-style change and an explicit Windows light/dark change while PowerToys Run is active, recording whether both reach ThemeManager.SetSystemTheme.

Compare the requested ThemeMode with the current application mode and test whether skipping an unchanged assignment prevents the duplicate-key exception; retain a different fix path if the duplicate occurs without redundant assignments.
Add focused coverage for repeated identical theme notifications and verify actual dark/light/high-contrast transitions still update the Run window.
verification: Repeat the trigger on the reported 0.87.1.0 build if available and on a current stable build.
Verify multiple identical General preference notifications do not throw, while genuine light/dark/high-contrast changes still update PowerToys Run.

confidence.rationale: The failing code path and duplicate key are directly identified, but the mouse-style trigger, product-area label, and old version do not establish that a redundant ThemeMode assignment is the cause.

issue_context.summary: A reported pointer-style change produces a WPF duplicate system-brush exception in PowerToys Run's system-theme refresh path.
known_information: The report gives version 0.87.1.0, Windows build 26200, and a stack trace for the exception.
The attached text contains the same duplicate SystemColorWindowColorBrush exception and PowerToys Run ThemeManager frames.
The issue has no discussion comments, assignees, or linked PR/duplicate references.
inferences: The WPF exception may be triggered by applying the same system ThemeMode more than once, but the stack alone does not prove that redundant assignment is necessary for the failure.
The described pointer-style action may cause a General system-preference notification, but this transition has not been verified.
issue_context.analysis: The stack is substantially more specific than the issue title and points to a fixable PowerToys Run theme-refresh path. The action therefore asks a maintainer to reproduce that path rather than requesting generic logs. The version and module/trigger mismatch keep confidence yellow.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body, labels, attachment link, discussion, and timeline; the issue is open, has no comments, and has no linked work.
Inspected the linked text attachment; it repeats the duplicate resource-key exception and Run ThemeManager call stack.
Checked current upstream ThemeManager.cs: General preference changes invoke UpdateTheme, and SetSystemTheme assigns Application.Current.ThemeMode each time.

actions.label: Approve focused Run theme fix investigation
actions.note: This approves a fork-side investigation only; the candidate is not a completed implementation-grade design.

reproduce.title: Verify the duplicate WPF resource during theme refresh
reproduce.version_requirement: First use the reported PowerToys 0.87.1.0 build if obtainable, then repeat on current stable; Windows 11 build 26200 is the reported environment.
prerequisites: Keep PowerToys Run active while changing a Windows user preference.
Record whether the pointer-style action also changes the Windows app theme or causes a General preference notification.
setup: Open the Windows pointer-style settings and the Windows Personalization > Colors page so the reported transition and a direct light/dark transition can be tested separately.
steps: With PowerToys Run active, change the pointer style to Inverted as described in the issue.
Repeat while changing the Windows app mode between Light and Dark.
Repeat an unchanged theme notification if it can be generated without changing the selected mode.
Check whether PowerToys Run logs the duplicate SystemColorWindowColorBrush exception and note which transition produces it.
reproduce.expected_result: No theme transition should throw the duplicate system-brush exception; genuine theme changes should still update PowerToys Run.
